observation.visible_scene: Against a pure black background, a small cylindrical perforated metal container (a mesh of round holes glowing warm orange from within) sits in the lower-right-center of the frame. On its flat top rests a dark, partially charred piece of fuel (a flat sliver of wood/charcoal). A live fire burns on top of this fuel, with a bright yellow-white core and orange tongues of flame that rise and lean predominantly toward the upper-left. The camera and container stay fixed throughout; only the flame and the glow through the perforations change.
visible_changes: The flame body continuously flickers, changing height, width, and the angle of its leftward lean from frame to frame, sometimes tall and vertical, sometimes lower and stretched horizontally to the left.
Small detached wisps/sparks of flame repeatedly appear and vanish at the left edge of the main flame, drifting slightly away from it.
The brightness and shape of the white-hot core over the fuel shift as the flame licks across it.
The pattern of glowing dots through the container's perforations varies in intensity as the fire's light and the container's own burning contents fluctuate.
The dark fuel piece on top remains in the same position, but the flame wrapping around and over it deforms constantly.
outside_clip_unknowns: What the fuel material actually is and whether it is being added or consumed beyond this segment.
Whether the fire intensifies, weakens, or is extinguished after the last frame.
The setting/location outside the black backdrop and the full form of the container below the visible band.
uncertain_details: The exact cause of the leftward flame drift (air current vs. fuel geometry) is not determinable from the frames.
Some very faint detached flame fragments at the far left may be motion blur or genuine separate wisps; their precise nature is unclear.
Minor apparent changes in overall brightness could be flame flicker rather than any camera exposure shift.
